categories.label: State & Concurrency
categories.description: How Clojure systems manage data identity over time, mutable state, and asynchronous execution.

smells.name: Immutability Violation
smells.summary: Mutable state is used (e.g., redefining a def inside a function with def again) in a paradigm that emphasizes immutability.

smells.name: Blocking Inside Go
smells.summary: A blocking operation is used inside a go block.

smells.name: Nested Atoms
smells.summary: An Atom, Volatile, or Ref is stored inside another Atom.

smells.name: Misuse of Dynamic Scope
smells.summary: Dynamic variables (^:dynamic) and binding are used to carry application state or resources.

smells.name: Overengineering with core.async
smells.summary: clojure.core.async channels are used for simple single-value asynchronous tasks.

smells.name: Dynamically-Scoped Singleton Resource
smells.summary: Critical resources are passed through dynamic variables and binding.

smells.name: Unnecessary Laziness
smells.summary: Lazy sequence functions (map, filter) are used where eager alternatives (mapv, into []) would suffice.

categories.label: Environment & Idioms
categories.description: How Clojure code interacts with the language's core abstractions, runtime behavior, and idiomatic conventions.

smells.name: Unmanaged Resource I/O
smells.summary: with-open is not used when handling resources that implement java.io.Closeable.

smells.name: Relying on Load-Time Side Effects
smells.summary: Code depends on top-level forms evaluated during namespace loading.

smells.name: Namespace Load Side Effects
smells.summary: require or requiring-resolve is called in a top-level form outside the primary ns macro.

smells.name: Multiple Evaluation in Macros
smells.summary: A macro inserts an input argument form into generated code more than once without first binding it to a gensym local variable.

smells.name: Direct usage of clojure.lang.RT
smells.summary: Methods from the internal clojure.lang.RT class are called directly.

smells.name: Unnecessary Macros
smells.summary: Macros are used where simpler functions or existing language constructs would suffice.

smells.name: Production doall
smells.summary: doall is used to force realization of lazy sequences.

smells.name: Misuse of Channel Closing Semantics
smells.summary: A sentinel value is used to signal channel termination instead of a/close!.

smells.name: Refs in Dependency Vector
smells.summary: A mutable reference object (Atom, use-state, raw use-ref) is placed directly into a hook's dependency array instead of its dereferenced value (@ref).

smells.name: Improper Emptiness Check
smells.summary: Verbose constructs like (not (empty? x)) or (when-not (empty? x) ...).

smells.name: Unnecessary into
smells.summary: `into` is used where more concise idiomatic alternatives exist.

categories.label: Module Boundaries & Data Contracts
categories.description: The surface area of namespaces and modules, and the clarity and predictability of values exchanged across them.

smells.name: Monolithic Namespace Split
smells.summary: A single logical namespace is split across multiple physical files using load and in-ns.

smells.name: Implicit Namespace Dependencies
smells.summary: Broad namespace imports (:use, :refer :all) or indirectly loaded namespaces are used.

smells.name: Marker Protocol
smells.summary: `defprotocol` is used solely as a type marker for type checking instead of defining polymorphic behavior.

smells.name: Single-segment Namespace
smells.summary: Single-segment namespaces are used.

smells.name: Private Multimethods
smells.summary: A defmulti or its defmethod`s are marked private.

smells.name: Non-Idiomatic Record Construction
smells.summary: Java interop constructor syntax (e.g., (Foo. 1 2)) is used to instantiate a defrecord or deftype

smells.name: Excessive Refers
smells.summary: A namespace explicitly refers a large number of Vars or uses (:refer :all).

smells.name: Map With Nil Values
smells.summary: `nil` values are inserted into maps.

smells.name: Non-Idiomatic Parameter Binding
smells.summary: Confusing syntax like & [x] is used to define a single optional argument.

categories.label: Logic Flow & Readability
categories.description: The visual and cognitive path through which data transformations are expressed in code.

smells.name: Conditional Build-Up
smells.summary: State is incrementally constructed through a series of let, if, and assoc expressions.

smells.name: Nested Forms
smells.summary: Multiple binding/iteration forms (let, when-let, if-let, doseq) are unnecessarily nested.

smells.name: Misused Threading
smells.summary: Threading macros (-> or ->>) are used to chain operations where the data type changes fundamentally at each step (e.g., map -> string -> File -> map).

smells.name: Case with Non-Literal Test Values
smells.summary: The `case` macro is used with runtime values (bindings or variables) as test expressions.

smells.name: Thread Ignorance
smells.summary: Threading macros (->, ->>, some->, cond->) are avoided where they would simplify data flow

smells.name: Verbose Checks
smells.summary: Manual comparisons are used instead of idiomatic predicate functions.

smells.name: Redundant do block
smells.summary: A do block is used inside constructs with an implicit do.
